title: Filesystem-controlled event fields allow terminal escape and output-spoofing injection
reasoning: Finding titles, evidence paths, commands, recommendations, and generic details are printed without filtering control characters. Repository filenames can contain escape, carriage-return, and newline characters, so an untrusted repository can emit ANSI or OSC sequences, overwrite displayed status, forge COMPLETE/STOPPED lines, or trigger terminal features such as clipboard operations.
reproduction: Render a finding whose evidence path contains an ESC-prefixed ANSI or OSC sequence, or a newline followed by a forged COMPLETE line. The raw control characters are returned and printed unchanged.
recommendation: Centralize terminal-safe rendering for all externally derived event fields. Escape C0/C1 terminal controls and safely indent or annotate embedded line breaks while preserving newlines introduced by the renderer itself.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were supplied, and there is no visible adversarial rendering coverage for control characters or hostile filenames.
suggestedRegressionTest: Pass events containing ESC, BEL, carriage return, and embedded newlines in titles, paths, commands, and details; assert no raw terminal-control sequence or unindented forged status line reaches the rendered output.
minimumFixScope: Add one terminal-sanitization helper and apply it to all event-derived values in _render_inspection and _render_event.
